title: Good every time, safe for everyone, proven to work
course_title: Training-of-Trainers (ToT): Teach Adults and Build Trainers

say: Good every time, safe for everyone, and proven to work.
This is the video for module three of the Training-of-Trainers course.
Quality means participants reach the objectives and leave able to do something new. It does not mean beautiful slides.
A weak session is easy to spot in the first hour. The trainer talks most of the time, nobody practises, and it runs over.

right: Participants active most of the time

say: In a strong session, participants are active, there are three to five clear objectives, they practise with coaching, and it ends on time with a check.

say: Fidelity means delivering the training as designed. In a cascade, a trainer who changes key messages may spread wrong information. But some adaptation is healthy.
So mark every part of your trainer guide as core or flexible.

say: Do no harm. A money discussion could make a husband suspicious, so use a fictional case story instead of asking for personal experiences on sensitive topics.

cards.d: Collect only what you need, say why, store it securely, report totals not names.

Listen calmly, no secret promises, tell the safeguarding focal person. Never investigate.

say: Transport refunds cause mistrust. Say clearly what is provided, pay everyone the same way, and record every payment with a signature, thumbprint or transfer receipt.

say: If a participant shares that she or her child is being harmed, listen calmly and do not push for details. Do not promise to keep a secret. Inform your safeguarding focal person promptly, and never investigate on your own.
Find out who that person is before every training.

say: People enjoyed it is a start, not proof. Level one is reaction: a short feedback form, with smiley faces for low-literacy groups.

panel.heading: Four levels of evaluation
items: Reaction: was it useful? End of session
Learning: same test before and after
Behaviour: using it? 4 to 12 weeks later
Results: outcomes, 3 to 12 months later

say: Level two is learning: the same short test before and after, linked to your objectives.

panel.heading: Four levels of evaluation
items: Reaction: was it useful? End of session
Learning: same test before and after
Behaviour: using it? 4 to 12 weeks later
Results: outcomes, 3 to 12 months later

say: Level three is behaviour: a follow-up call or visit 4 to 12 weeks later. Plan it before the training starts.

say: Level four is results, like savings totals, 3 to 12 months later. Many things affect results, so describe your contribution carefully.

say: For example, Ngozi trains 20 traders in Onitsha with a 10-question test. Before training, the scores add up to 80. 80 divided by 20 is an average of 4.0 out of 10.

panel.heading: Calculating learning gain
items: Pre-test: 80 / 20 = 4.0 out of 10
Post-test: 160 / 20 = 8.0 out of 10
Change: 40 percentage points
Six weeks later: 12 of 18 reached record daily

say: After training, the scores add up to 160. That is an average of 8.0 out of 10.

panel.heading: Calculating learning gain
items: Pre-test: 80 / 20 = 4.0 out of 10
Post-test: 160 / 20 = 8.0 out of 10
Change: 40 percentage points
Six weeks later: 12 of 18 reached record daily

say: So the average went from 40 percent to 80 percent, an increase of 40 percentage points.

panel.rule: Say how many you reached and how you checked. Honesty builds trust.

say: To remember. Mark content core or flexible. Observe with a short scored checklist. Use fictional cases for sensitive topics. Know your safeguarding focal person. And evaluate at four levels, reporting honestly, including the limits.
